clue.text: Married in a fit of lunacy? That's slander

indicators.note: the letter for married is placed in among the shaken-up letters
a fit is a wild outburst, so the letters of lunacy are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether marrying was madness, and is told that remark is slanderous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fit of' rearranges LUNACY into CALUNY, and 'in' puts M among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a false spoken statement that damages a person's reputation.

clue.text: Girl able to set up a whole lot of dates

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: to be able is to be capable, i.e. can

explanation.surface: A capable girl arranges a busy calendar of dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns CAN into NAC beneath ALMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly almanac is a calendar listing many dates and events.

clue.text: Take away gun from a French member

parts.note: un is the French masculine word for a
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone is disarmed by a French soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of weapons is to disarm them, an older synonym.

clue.text: Irregular deliveries

parts.note: in cricket an illegal ball bowled by the bowler gives the batting side an extra run; the surface suggests faulty postal deliveries

explanation.surface: Parcels arriving at odd times.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and one bowled illegally (for example overstepping the crease) is penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket deliveries ruled illegal by the umpire carry this name, so they are literally irregular.

clue.text: Antique chair that's broken must be taken into account

indicators.note: the shaken letters are placed inside the abbreviation for account
a broken chair is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An antique dealer's broken chair has to be written off in the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's broken' rearranges CHAIR into RCHAI; the account abbreviation AC wraps round it, as 'must be taken into' asks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very old and out of date, like an antique, is called archaic.

clue.text: One may take it as a safe place

definitions.text: One may take it as a safe place

parts.words: One may take it as a safe place
parts.note: people take shelter, or take it, in a safe place, the surface hinting at regarding something as safe

explanation.surface: Someone may consider something a safe bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter where people go for safety, as in taking sanctuary.

clue.text: Breathe irregularly at what should be regular

indicators.note: breathing irregularly scrambles the letters out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone gasps unevenly, worrying about a pulse that ought to be steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' rearranges BREATHE into HEARTBE; AT follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A healthy pulse of the heart ought to keep a steady rhythm.

clue.text: This turned out to sum up Panama, for example

indicators.note: turned out means the letters have been turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A summary of Panama turns out to be simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges THIS and SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a narrow strip of land joining two larger landmasses, the classic example of this geographical feature.

clue.text: Prince rather upset, having to accept a royal spouse

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters take in the single letter, enclosing it
upset means knocked over, so the letters of the two words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A prince is upset because he must take on a royal wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges PRINCE and RATHER, and 'having to accept' takes A into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr was the sixth and last wife of Henry VIII, so a queen consort.

clue.text: Nelson held her in high esteem, maybe

indicators.note: the name sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson admired a certain woman greatly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across esteEM MAybe. Lord Nelson's lover was Emma Hamilton, whom he held in his arms as well as in his esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Hamilton, Nelson's famous mistress, bore this first name.

clue.text: Parties of runners?

parts.note: runners suggests athletes, but runner beans are the meant sense, and a party of them is a feast of beans

explanation.surface: Celebrations held by athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: A beanfeast is British slang for a jolly party; the clue reads it literally as a feast of runner beans.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a celebration or jolly, originally an employer's annual dinner.

clue.text: Horse, for example, backed for plate

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the word for plate is read in reverse

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse in a race for a trophy plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns LAMINA around.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is one example of a creature of the beast kingdom.

clue.text: Drunk given prison sentence none too soon

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated
doing time means serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A drunk is finally jailed, and not before time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something is overdue, happening not a moment too early.

clue.text: An additional dress item for an accomplice

definitions.meaning: a handbag or scarf added to an outfit
in law, one who helps another commit a crime

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an extra fashion item and a person who assists a criminal.

clue.text: Save excerpt of novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a passage from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges EXCERPT OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Save in the sense of apart from or but is a preposition meaning the same as this phrase.

clue.text: Finish with conclusion of judge in lawsuit

indicators.note: the final letter goes inside the word for lawsuit

parts.note: a case is a legal action brought in court

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A lawsuit ends with the judge's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion of' gives E from judge, and 'in' puts it inside CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to stop or come to an end, a direct synonym.

clue.text: He tangles with cop — that will mean time

indicators.note: a tangle mixes things up, so the letters are knotted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who scuffles with a policeman will end up doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangles with' rearranges HE and COP.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a period or era of history, a span of time.

clue.text: Be mother for the French, when abroad

parts.note: pour is the French word for for
abroad can mean out and about, outside

explanation.surface: An expatriate mother living in France.
explanation.walkthrough: To be mother is a British idiom for pouring out the tea for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving tea from the pot at a gathering is the meaning of the British idiom.

clue.text: Son traces scattered family members

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A son looks up relatives spread far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges SON TRACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears are relatives from earlier generations of a family.

clue.text: Last but not least

parts.note: the familiar phrase for a final mention also describes something both final and of the greatest degree

explanation.surface: The stock phrase used when introducing the final item.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both the very end (the extreme point) and the greatest degree, the opposite of least.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the furthest end and the utmost intensity.

clue.text: Censure about the degree of alcohol

parts.note: re means about or concerning
proof is the measure of a spirit's alcoholic strength

explanation.surface: Disapproval of how strong the drink is.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuke or expression of blame is a synonym for censure.

clue.text: Road is renovated — it is skilfully done

indicators.note: something renovated is remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A road has been resurfaced, and the job is neatly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovated' rearranges ROAD into ADRO; IT follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft and clever with the hands, as work that is skilfully carried out.

clue.text: Leaped — above oneself?

definitions.meaning: conceited, having ideas above one's station

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both sprang upward and, as an adjective, self-important and upstart.

clue.text: Vagrants responsible for swindle in backstreet

indicators.note: the swindle word goes inside the reversed street abbreviation

parts.note: ST, the abbreviation for street, read backwards gives TS
a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket

explanation.surface: Homeless people are blamed for a con in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'back' inside backstreet is the reversing signal on ST. RAMP is old British slang for a con or racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are homeless wanderers, the same as vagrants.

clue.text: A danger out East at this time of the year

indicators.note: out means the letter for East is taken out

parts.note: a peril is a danger
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A warning of danger out in the East at this season.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'A danger out East' sound like a travel warning; 'out' actually ejects the compass letter, leaving PRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The month is one particular time of the year, defined vaguely.

clue.text: It's designed for handicapped drivers to do the rounds

definitions.text: It's designed for handicapped drivers to do the rounds

parts.words: It's designed for handicapped drivers to do the rounds
parts.note: golfers have handicaps, drivers are clubs, and they play rounds; the surface suggests disabled motorists

explanation.surface: A route laid out for disabled motorists making their rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf terms: a handicap is a player's rating, a driver a long-hitting club, and a round a full game.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout of holes where golfers with handicaps play rounds.

clue.text: Area said to be uncultivated

indicators.note: said signals the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: rude in its old sense means rough, unrefined

explanation.surface: A patch of land reported to be untilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is an old unit of land area, a quarter of an acre.

clue.text: Repeat treat that is arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)

explanation.surface: A treat is repeated by arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges TREAT and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: To say or do again is a direct synonym of repeat.

clue.text: Rich source no longer available

parts.note: a well is a source of water
a dish that is off the menu is no longer available

explanation.surface: A rich supply that has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthy or prosperous is the meaning of this phrase.
